claims.statement: Algolia documents a Write API key among the keys assigned to a team member, and indexing keys that add or delete records and manage indices.

sources.supports: Depending on the permissions you give this team member, the API keys can include: Search-only API key, Write API key, Admin API key.

claims.statement: Algolia states that write-access keys must not be used in frontend code or mobile apps.

sources.supports: Don't use write-access keys in frontend code or mobile apps, and use environment variables for API keys in your code instead of hardcoding them.

claims.statement: No provider page read states the value shape of Algolia API keys. Two pinned open-source scanner rule artifacts, written by different maintainers, are both consistent with a 32-character alphanumeric value that appears near the word "algolia" being an Algolia API key candidate. Neither artifact distinguishes admin, search-only or write role from the value, and this claim is consistency with observed practice, not a statement about what Algolia issues.

sources.supports: The rule builds a semi-generic pattern from the keyword "algolia" and the body pattern [a-z0-9]{32} (case-insensitive in the generated configuration), with "algolia" as its keyword.
The detector pairs the keywords "algolia", "docsearch" and "apiKey" with the body pattern [a-zA-Z0-9]{32} delimited by word boundaries, with "algolia" and "docsearch" as its keywords.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: This candidate is established only as existing: the prefix, alphabet, length and structure of the value are not documented on the pages read and are not researched.

The pages read do not say whether Algolia keys of different roles share one value shape; role must not be attributed from shape alone, and identification needs the surrounding context (header, variable name, ACL).
Whether the predefined Write API key and a custom key whose ACL grants write actions (addObject, deleteObject, editSettings) are one credential family or two is not settled by the pages read.

The 32-character alphanumeric shape is only tool-corroborated by two scanner rule artifacts and is not stated by Algolia; whether every key of this role has that shape, and whether any other key kind shares it, is not established. The two artifacts are not checked beyond their rule text, and a reviewer should confirm their authorship is independent.
